title: Delhi Bus Journey Planner — Team DROIDERS (Shivam Bansal)

beats.caption: Hi everyone, I'm Shivam Bansal from Team DROIDERS. Today I'm showing how we solved real-world bus travel-time prediction and journey planning for Delhi over 560M cleaned GPS pings: OTP2 proposes routes while our causal engine owns timing, [p10, p90] windows, transfer risk, and honest abstention.
beats.tts_text: Hi everyone, I am Shivam Bansal from Team Droiders. Today I am showing you how we solved real world bus travel time prediction and journey planning for Delhi. Standard timetables break down in heavy traffic and hide uncertainty. Using five hundred sixty million cleaned GPS pings, Open Trip Planner proposes candidate routes, while our causal engine owns bus timing, ten to ninety percentile arrival windows, transfer risk, and honest abstention.

beats.caption: Starting in real time from Kashmere Gate ISBT to Nehru Place: live GTFS-RT positions from active Delhi buses, arrival windows, late-night comparisons, and per-leg provenance.
beats.tts_text: Let us start with a real time journey from Kashmere Gate ISBT to Nehru Place. Our planner pulls fresh GPS positions from active Delhi buses, displaying realistic arrival windows, comparisons against late night traffic, and clear data sources for every leg.

beats.caption: Switching to Oct 22 replay on route 717A with a strict causal cutoff: our LightGBM + split-conformal model cuts held-out MAE by 31% (87.3 s -> 60.2 s) with 79.2% [p10, p90] coverage.
beats.tts_text: Next, let us switch to October twenty second replay on route seven seventeen A, using a strict causal cutoff at departure time. Our Light GBM and split conformal model cuts held out mean absolute error by thirty one percent, dropping from eighty seven point three down to sixty point two seconds, with seventy nine point two percent interval coverage.

beats.caption: Replaying a corridor outside route 717A: with no replay observations covering candidate routes, the planner refuses to guess and abstains with "Not enough data".
beats.tts_text: Now watch what happens when we replay a corridor outside route seven seventeen A. Because there are no replay observations covering those routes, the planner refuses to guess and clearly abstains with Not enough data.

beats.caption: For routes outside 717A, PR #28 adds a causal per-stretch, per-day scalar Kalman ratio filter: across 16,247 held-out stretches on 6 busy routes, offline MAE drops from 80.3 s to 57.3 s (28.6% gain vs timetable).
beats.tts_text: So how do we improve accuracy on routes outside seven seventeen A? In pull request twenty eight, we added a causal scalar Kalman filter that tracks each road segment every day using travel time ratios. Across sixteen thousand two hundred forty seven held out segments on six busy routes, it cuts offline mean absolute error from eighty point three down to fifty seven point three seconds, a twenty eight point six percent improvement over the timetable on October data.

beats.caption: Why real-time transfer risk matters (Oct 22 GPS, run 2171): the timetable recommends transferring at Hamdard Nagar, then incoming GPS delay pushes the buffer into risk.
beats.tts_text: Now let us see why real time transfer risk matters, replaying actual October twenty second GPS for run twenty one seventy one. At departure, the timetable recommends a transfer at Hamdard Nagar. Just minutes later, incoming GPS delay eats into the buffer and pushes that connection into the danger zone.

beats.caption: At Tuglaqabad, advice flips to the direct 717A bus before boarding. Stage 4 reveals the true Oct 22 GPS outcome: the connecting bus left 27m 43s before 717A arrived.
beats.tts_text: By the time the bus reaches Tuglaqabad, our planner flips its advice to the direct seven seventeen A bus before the rider commits. Stage four reveals what truly happened that evening: the connecting bus had already departed twenty-seven minutes and forty-three seconds before the seven seventeen A bus arrived.

beats.caption: Pausing the poller past the 45 s demo threshold triggers a stale-GPS abstention, blocking outdated estimates with exact provenance.
beats.tts_text: A trustworthy planner also knows when its own GPS feed goes stale. Here we pause the background poller past our forty five second freshness threshold, and the interface immediately blocks outdated predictions with the exact abstention code and timestamp.

beats.caption: Resuming polling and re-running the query immediately restores fresh live routes.
beats.tts_text: The moment we resume polling and run the query again, freshness checks pass and real time routes return automatically.

beats.caption: Nov 25 5-hour live check (177 matched 717A legs): 227.5 s vs 393.3 s timetable MAE, 96.6% [p10, p90] coverage. Built by Shivam Bansal and Team DROIDERS.
beats.tts_text: To validate everything in the real world, we ran a five hour morning field check on November twenty fifth across one hundred seventy seven matched bus rides on route seven seventeen A. Our model beat the timetable at two hundred twenty seven point five seconds versus three hundred ninety three point three seconds mean absolute error, with ninety six point six percent coverage. Causal, calibrated, and honest, built by Shivam Bansal and Team Droiders. Thanks for watching.
